subject: Post-call recap: ACME discovery & integration fit (SDK / streaming / embeddings)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-31T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: ACME discovery & integration fit (SDK / streaming / embeddings)

Jordan — great to meet earlier. Quick recap of what we discussed, the problems you called out, and recommended next steps.

Pain points / goals:
- High 95th-percentile latency for interactive search assistant (target <= 300ms Token Round Trip)
- Need deterministic, paginated embeddings pipeline for semantic search + reranking
- Avoid lock-in; want ability to run in our VPC for sensitive data later
- Budget sensitivity — cost per 1M tokens and per-embedding unit matters for sizing

Relevant Redwood capabilities we covered:
- Streaming + function calling for low-latency token production for the assistant
- Structured outputs to enforce JSON responses for downstream parsers
- Embeddings + reranking flow (offline embeddings -> ANN index -> recall + rerank using prompt scoring)
- Private deployment options (VPC) and Dedicated for predictable latency

Integration notes / ask from ACME:
- SDK languages: primary SDK is Node (server-side), some Python microservices
- Expected QPS: ~40 requests/s peak; average 12 req/s
- Typical sequence length: 350-600 tokens

Next steps (agreed):
1) Marissa to share a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) + estimated TCO delta for Dedicated vs Hosted by EOD Monday (see attached MAP)
2) ACME to share a representative prompt + 2 sample documents for an embeddings test index
3) Schedule a short tech deep-dive with your infra team (Vivek + Rafael suggested) — proposed Tue 6/2 10am PT

Attachments:
- redwood-acme-map.xlsx (mutual action plan)
- integration-diagram.pdf (high-level SDK flow)

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed anything.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Jordan Smith <jordan@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ACME discovery & integration fit (SDK / streaming / embeddings)

Thanks Marissa — this is great, appreciate the thorough recap.

A couple quick clarifications:
- For latency: the 300ms target is for end-to-end token turn time from our app edge to final token. Can you confirm whether the Dedicated SLA covers p50/p95 per-token latency for streams?
- For embeddings pricing: do you have a ballpark e$/embed for a quantized 8-bit embedding model vs hosted accounts? Would like a rough comparison in the MAP.

I'll get the sample prompt and two docs over by EOD today. Tue 6/2 10am PT works for the tech deep-dive; looping in our infra lead (samia@acme.com) separately.

-Jordan

Thanks — quick answers inline and updated MAP attached.

- SLA/latency: Dedicated provides an SLA for availability and backing latency targets. For streaming per-token p95 we typically see ~220-320ms depending on model/sequence length; we'll include model-specific estimates in the MAP. Rafael will follow up with a short note on kernel/quantization choices that impact that envelope.
- Embedding pricing: In the MAP we included two cost rows: Hosted (multi-tenant) e.g. $X / 1k embeddings, Dedicated (reserved) estimates that reduce per-embed unit by ~30% at our projected volumes. I'll add a little footnote comparing 8-bit quantized runs vs fp16 for inference cost delta.

- Rafael: write 2–3 bullets on model/quantization choices for the tech deep-dive (by EOD Mon)
